reason: E2 directly shows that a Ti-rich surface film forms and provides passivation and high corrosion resistance in Mg-Ti-Zn alloys, supporting the Ti segregation and protection premises. E1 describes layered oxide formation and elemental segregation in a different alloy system (CoCrFeNiMn) at a lower temperature, which provides only generic support for diffusion-driven surface enrichment but does not involve Ti or Mg. The specific claim about Ti dominating over Mg and forming a continuous TiO₂ layer at 600 °C is not directly evidenced by the cited passages.
premises: Ti has higher oxygen affinity than Mg and will selectively segregate to the surface during oxidation at 600 °C
A continuous TiO₂-rich oxide layer forms and is protective/passivating
This TiO₂ layer reduces corrosion rates despite the presence of Mg
The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports selective Ti segregation and protective Ti-rich film formation in Mg-containing alloys
